clauses.reason: The only operative command of EO 6654 is the approval of an amendment of the Lumber and Timber Products Industries code, in the President's words 'do adopt and approve the report of the Administrator recommending the granting of the aforesaid application, and do order that the Code of Fair Competition for the Lumber and Timber Products Industries, as approved by me on August 19, 1933, be amended in accordance with the foregoing'. The order acts under Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act on an application under that Act, so the command is a section 3 amendment of an approved code whose operative effect depended on the code-approval provisions of Title I. No earlier end applies: the order states no period, condition or provisional approval, and no held record shows the code or its amendments cancelled or suspended before June 14, 1935 (see earlier_end_check). The command ended on June 14, 1935, when Congress approved S.J. Res. 113 (49 Stat. 375); its section 2 provides 'All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed'. The resolution states no effective date other than its approval and nothing defers section 2, so June 14, 1935 is the end of the prospective operative effect of the amendment approval. Schechter (May 27, 1935) is a validity characterization, not an end date; June 16, 1935 is not an end because section 1 of the resolution replaced that expiry with April 1, 1936. Actor: Congress, by S.J. Res. 113 section 2.

research_rationale:
EO 6654 (signed March 23, 1934, Franklin D. Roosevelt) approves, on the application of the Lumber Code Authority, an amendment of the Code of Fair Competition for the Lumber and Timber Products Industries, and modifies the approval accordingly; the application is described as carrying out the forest conservation provisions of Article X of the code. The code was approved by EO 6255 of August 19, 1933. Identity: the census register row, the WPA 1944 numbered list entry at p. 572 and the held text agree on number, date and subject. Source: the American Presidency Project transcription (a Common Crawl capture, grade mirror_transcription, acceptable_as_original false); the page record with the same sha256 names this order's number, its date and subject agree with the text, and its text_sha256 is the held text's. The claim follows the reviewed shared analysis of NIRA code approvals: an amendment of an approved code is a section 3 command whose operative effect ended on June 14, 1935 by statutory repeal (S.J. Res. 113 section 2); Schechter recorded as a validity characterization, not an end date; accrued effects survive as past effects.

savings.reason: Nothing continues the approval after the repeal. Acts done and liabilities incurred under the code as amended by this order before June 14, 1935 are accrued consequences, not continued operation of EO 6654. The section 5 antitrust exemption for action taken while the code was in effect is likewise an accrued effect for that past action; the resolution's proviso reads 'Provided, That the exemption provided in section 5 of such title shall extend only to agreements and action thereunder', names agreements rather than codes and states no time limit, and the held text does not settle how far it narrowed the exemption for past action under codes. No held source shows a prosecution continued or any action under the code taken after June 14, 1935.

source_notes.date_qualification: 1935-05-27: date the section 3 delegation was declared unconstitutional; validity characterization (void from issuance under then-prevailing doctrine), not an end date
source_notes.reason: Schechter, 295 U.S. 495, held the code provisions in question invalid on the delegation ground and on the intrastate-commerce ground. It is recorded as a validity characterization of every section 3 code approval (void from issuance under the doctrine prevailing in 1935), not as an end of this order; the judgment did not cancel or withdraw this approval.

source_notes.date_qualification: 1933-06-16: enactment date of the National Industrial Recovery Act; not an end date
source_notes.reason: Section 3 of Title I states the legal effects of an approved code that section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 repealed by description: under 3(b) its provisions are the standards of fair competition for the trade or industry, under 3(c) the district courts may restrain violations, and under 3(f) a violation is a misdemeanor. Cited for the content of the repealed provisions, not for any date.
